3.text: near the mouth of the Konkova River. We were starving. So he, Daniel,

4.text: sent us by tundra to the winter hamlet (зимовье) of the Lower Kolyma. We

5.text: lost our way and fed on weeds, and reached the Kolyma on the tenth day,

6.text: where we found Cossacks occupied with fishing. There we have staid until

7.text: this present year 1710. In January of this year some Chukchee robbers came

8.text: with deceit to the Lower Kolyma winter hamlet. One of them was taken

9.text: captive, Niˊtkal, according to his Chukchee name. The said Niˊtkal said that

10.text: Daniel Busormanov, going by sea, did not recognize the mouth of the Kolyma,

11.text: and passed beyond as far as the mouth of the Big River; and there the

12.text: Shelag Chukchee murdered him and his comrades.”¹ This is the first direct

13.text: mention of the unknown Shelag, much earlier than that by Wrangell.²

14.text: Still more interesting is the report of Sept. 2, 1711, presented in the

15.text: fortress of Anadyrsk, in the judicial chamber (судная изба), to the officer

16.text: Matthew Skrebykin by the serving-man Popov, who was sent to the Chukchee

17.text: Land to collect information concerning the Chukchee, and also to invite them

19.text: The report says, “He [Popov] and the Anadyr hunter George Toldin,

20.text: and the newly baptized Yukaghir Ivan Tereshkin, went from the mouth of

21.text: the Anadyr to Chukchee Cape. And those unpeaceful Chukchee said that

22.text: before that the Russian men had come to them by sea,³ but they had paid

23.text: them no tribute. Likewise at the present time they would not pay anything,

24.text: nor would they give hostages . . . And from that cape he came with his

25.text: comrades to the Anadyr River, and collected tribute from the River Chukchee

26.text: Nokon and his comrades, — five red foxes, one fox from every man. The

27.text: Reindeer Chukchee live on the cape along the hills. The ‘walking’ Chukchee

28.text: live on both sides of the cape, in earthen houses along the spits, near the

29.text: sea, where the walrus dwell . . . According to their custom, the Chukchee,

30.text: when concluding an agreement, call on the Sun as a witness.

31.text: “And opposite that Anadyr Cape, on both sides of the Kolyma Sea

32.text: and of the Anadyr Sea, there is to be seen an island. About that island, the

33.text: Cape Chukchee Makachkin and his kinsmen have told him for quite certain

34.text: that there live upon that island (large) toothed people. Their religion and

35.text: customs and language are different from those of the Chukchee, and since

36.text: ancient times there has been no peace between the Cape Chukchee and those

37.text: island people. They attack each other and fight. The fighting of the islanders

38.text: is with bows, and of the Chukchee the same. Of those island people he has

39.text: seen among the Chukchee about ten or more taken captive. Besides their

40.text: natural teeth, they have small pieces of walrus-ivory put in through the cheeks
